conviction_note: abs_move 10.0 (event-implied 9.51, median of 7 own reactions 8.0, and a Q4 guide is at stake) x (2*0.56-1) = +1.2. The lean rests on the company's own tariff assumption: incremental tariffs of 20% RoW / 30% China, with a $35m benefit the CFO said was not in guidance, against Section 122 at 10% and Section 301 at 10-12.5% since 24 July. That leaves room to raise the FY guide. p_up is held at 56 rather than 60+ because this name has sold its last two beats (-12.55% Oct 2025, -2.17% Jul 2026), the skew already pays for upside, and peer demand in the June-August quarter was flat. The findings sum (+2.1) and the scaled number (+1.2) agree in sign. The gap between them is the reaction-function discount carried in p_up.

findings.finding: Levi's FY26 guide assumes incremental US tariffs of 20% on rest-of-world and 30% on China, and on the Q2 call the CFO said a ~$35m tariff benefit is not in guidance because he expected rates to go back to 19-20% in late July. Instead Section 122 (10%) was replaced on 24 July by Section 301 duties of 10% (Mexico, Bangladesh, Cambodia, India, Indonesia, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, Guatemala and others) or 12.5% (Vietnam and most others). The guide carries cost headroom that points to a raised FY gross margin/EPS outlook (~$0.07/share for the $35m alone) and a firmer Q4 implied guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance raises were bought: +10.65% (2026-04-07, Q1 beat and FY raise), +11.25% (2025-07-10). A raise whose midpoint sat below consensus was sold: -2.17% (2026-07-08, FY $1.46-1.52 against ~$1.51 FactSet, Q3 decel guide). A margin/tariff guide disappointment fell -12.55% (2025-10-09).
findings.why_not_priced: If the market were paying for a tariff-driven raise, the stock would not be down ~17-20% since the July beat-and-raise while the S&P rose 4%, the forward P/E would not be ~12.6x, and previews would cite tariff headroom. They cite 'tariff pressure' as a risk (TradingKey 2026-10-02). It is partly priced: analysts asked about the $35m on the call, and the skew already leans upside.
findings.independence: Tariff rates come from a different source: Morgan Lewis 2026-07-27 (https://www.morganlewis.com/pubs/2026/07/us-administration-rebuilds-global-tariff-program-under-section-301), which gives Section 122 at 10% to 24 July and Section 301 at 10%/12.5% after it. The assumption itself is in the Q2 press release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000094845/000009484526000038/exhibit991-2q2026pressrele.htm). Peers' tariff lines also improved: H&M Q3 gross margin +1.6pp from one-time tariff effects (https://pulse2.com/hm-group-reports-23-increase-in-third-quarter-operating-profit-to-609-million/).

findings.finding: Levi paid ~$80m of IEEPA tariffs and at 31 May had recognised a refund asset only for CAPE phase 1 (10-Q note 9). The CFO said most of its refunds run through reconciliation entries, and CAPE Phase 2, which covers reconciliation-flagged entries, opened on 29 June, inside fiscal Q3 (1 June-30 August). A refund recognition of tens of millions in Q3 GAAP results is therefore likely, excluded from adjusted EPS as Gap's $417m was.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior Levi refund print. Peers recognised refunds excluded from adjusted (Gap $417m in its August quarter). Across this repo's runs the tariff-refund names split by the direction of guidance, not by the refund.
findings.why_not_priced: It is excluded from guidance and from adjusted EPS, so consensus carries none of it. Its only path to value is cash (~$60m after tax, under 1% of a ~$7.8bn market cap) and buybacks ($240m authorisation remaining). That path is real but small, so it is sized at a fraction of the same money as operating profit.
findings.independence: Phase 2 date and scope: Thompson Hine 2026-06-25 (https://www.thompsonhinesmartrade.com/2026/06/cbp-confirms-june-29-2026-ieepa-tariff-refund-process-phase-2-launch/). Peer precedent: Gap Q2 (https://www.just-style.com/newsletters/gap-q2-profit-outperforms-projections-on-tariff-refund-despite-sales-drop). The 'reconciliation' remark shares the Q2 transcript with finding 1.

findings.finding: Management called the Q3 step-down to +4-5% 'prudence' and 'conservatism' rather than demand deterioration, and said quarter-to-date trends supported the outlook. Levi beat EPS in Q1 (+$0.05) and Q2 (+$0.04, revenue +2.8% vs consensus). With consensus pinned at the top of the guide, a modest beat on revenue and EPS is the base case.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Beats have been sold on this name: 2025-10-09 a beat fell -12.55%, and 2026-07-08 a beat-and-raise closed -2.17% after opening ~-6% (shopappy). A plain beat is not what this stock pays for.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus at $0.36 is already the top of the guide, so a beat of 1-2 cents is the market's expectation. Only a larger beat would be new. This is mostly priced.
findings.independence: Beat record: AAII 2026-10-06 (https://www.aaii.com/investingideas/article/511490-what-you-need-to-know-about-levi-strauss--cos-q3-earnings) and Q1 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/94845/000009484526000021/exhibit991-1q2026pressrele.htm). Shares the transcript with findings 1 and 2.

findings.finding: Peer and counterparty demand over Levi's exact quarter was flat to soft. H&M June-August sales were +1% in local currencies with September guided +1%. Kontoor's Wrangler US wholesale was flat. Gap's Old Navy comps were -4% (Gap brand +10%), Kohl's comps -0.9%, and American Eagle brand comps -1%. That gives little reason to expect Levi's wholesale to run well above its own cautious +4-5% guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2026-07-08 reaction (-2.17%, opening ~-6%) was attributed to the Q3 growth deceleration and 'cautious consumer spending and uneven apparel demand'.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the stock is -17% since July against S&P +4%, consistent with the market having absorbed soft apparel demand. Filed small because it is a proxy, and Levi's guide already embeds the deceleration.

Kohl's Q2: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000885639/000119312526365860/d171200dex991.htm. AEO: https://modernretail.co/operations/aerie-soars-in-back-to-school-sales-while-american-eagle-works-to-balance-denim. These are separate sources, but all are proxies.

findings.finding: This is CFO Harmit Singh's last print. John Vandemore becomes CFO on 1 November 2026, per the 8-K of 30 September, which carried no guidance reaffirmation. The Q4 guide is set by an outgoing CFO who already called the H2 plan conservative.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior CFO transition print in the baseline window.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public, and the retirement has been known since April 2026. Its only bearing is guide tone, and an incoming CFO starting after the print has little reason to sandbag it, so it is sized near zero.

outside_window.finding: Section 301 rates of 10-12.5% against the 20% assumed (plus 0% on qualifying CAFTA-DR/USMCA apparel) are a full-year FY27 gross-margin tailwind, given inventory turns of ~2x. They show up fully only in the FY27 guide in January 2027, though tone may surface on this call.
CAPE Phase 3 (finally liquidated entries, CIT plaintiffs only) deploys 2026-10-06, after Levi's Q3 closed. Any further IEEPA refund recognition for Levi lands in Q4 FY26, reported in January 2027.

baseline_tension: The positive lean agrees with the skew (-2.61, upside paid), so part of it is already in the price. It cuts against the 20-day run-up (-3.1%) and the -17% drift since July, which say the market has priced a soft quarter rather than a raise.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction): the reported-quarter beat finding cut from +0.8 to +0.4 because this name sold its last two beats; p_up moved from 58 to 56.
Rule 3 (your own caveat has to reach the number): the CFO-transition finding cut from -0.2 to -0.1, because its own why_not_priced argues there is little reason to sandbag.
Rule 2 (name the line; size one-offs as one-offs): the IEEPA refund stays a small one_off at +0.4 with no path to adjusted EPS. The tariff-assumption headroom stays a guidance finding at +2.0.
Rule 5 (a narrow proxy loses to a broad public series): the peer-demand proxy left at a small -0.6 and filed rather than dropped.

Rule 6 (verify the bar; keep findings inside the exit window): bar sourced to the company guide plus two agreeing estimates; the FY27 tariff tailwind and the Phase 3 refunds were already in outside_window.
